title_en: Puyang Hualong District Hualong Natural Gas Co., Ltd. v. Henan Province Puyang City Urban Management Bureau and Henan Province Puyang Municipal People's Government — retrial case regarding confirmation of invalidity of administrative agreement (arising from Puyang China Resources Gas Co., Ltd.’s lawsuit)
ruling_gist_en: An administrative agreement is an agreement concluded by an administrative authority with a citizen, legal person, or other organization through consultation for the purpose of achieving administrative management or public service objectives, and which contains rights and obligations under administrative law. A pipeline gas concession agreement, as a government concession agreement, is a typical administrative agreement that possesses both 'administrative nature' and 'contractual nature.' When hearing cases concerning the determination of the validity of an administrative agreement, the people's court shall not only review the agreement based on the circumstances of invalidity prescribed in the Administrative Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations, but also comply with the relevant civil legal norms for the determination of contract validity.

full_text_en:
Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. v. Puyang City Management Bureau of Henan Province, Puyang Municipal People's Government of Henan Province (Retrial Filed by Puyang Huolong District Hualong Natural Gas Co., Ltd.) — Dispute over Confirmation of Invalidity of Administrative Agreement

[Ruling Summary]

An administrative agreement is an agreement that a government agency enters into with a citizen, legal person, or other organization through negotiation for the purpose of achieving administrative management or public service objectives and that contains rights and obligations under administrative law. A pipeline gas concession agreement, as a government concession agreement, constitutes a typical administrative agreement that possesses both "administrative" and "contractual" characteristics. When a people's court hears a case concerning the determination of the validity of an administrative agreement, it must not only review the circumstances of invalidity as prescribed in the Administrative Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations, but also comply with the provisions of relevant civil legal norms regarding the determination of the validity of contracts.

Administrative Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2020) Supreme People's Court Admin. Retrial No. 509

Applicant for Retrial (Third Party at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Puyang Huolong District Hualong Natural Gas Co., Ltd., domiciled at No., Hualong Gas Distribution Station, South of East Section of Zhongyuan Road, Puyang City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Xue Yuan, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Tian Huagang, lawyer at Henan Jinmou Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Yahui, lawyer at Henan Jinmou Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Puyang City Management Bureau of Henan Province, domiciled at No. 112-2, Middle Section of Renmin Road, Puyang City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Hou Xianfeng, Director of the Bureau. Person in charge appearing in court: LYU Yingjie, Deputy Director of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Han Peishan, staff member of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Xue Feng, lawyer at Henan Puyang Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Puyang Municipal People's Government of Henan Province, domiciled at No. 158, Renmin Road, Huolong District, Puyang City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Wan Zhengfeng, Mayor of the Municipal People's Government.

Agent ad litem: Jin Aihong, staff member of the Municipal Judicial Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Li Jie, staff member of the Municipal Judicial Bureau.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 659, Middle Jinti Road, Puyang City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Guoyong, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Shi Huangian, lawyer at Henan Yingyu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Xinying, lawyer at Henan Dewenxing Law Firm.

The applicant for retrial, Puyang Huolong District Hualong Natural Gas Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hualong), dissatisfied with the administrative judgment (2018) Yu Xing Zhong No. 111 rendered by the Henan High People's Court in the case of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huarun) v. Puyang City Management Bureau of Henan Province (hereinafter referred to as Puyang City Management Bureau) and Puyang Municipal People's Government of Henan Province (hereinafter referred to as Puyang Municipal Government) concerning confirmation of invalidity of an administrative agreement, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered the administrative ruling (2019) Zui Gao Fa Xing Shen No. 13741 on November 24, 2020, granting the retrial of this case. After granting the retrial, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on September 10, 2021. The legal representative of the applicant for retrial, Hualong, Xue Yuan, and its agents ad litem, Tian Huagang; the responsible person of respondent Puyang City Management Bureau, LYU Yingjie, and its agents ad litem, Han Peishan and Xue Feng; the agents ad litem of respondent Puyang Municipal Government, Jin Aihong and Li Jie; and the agents ad litem of respondent Huarun, Shi Huangian and Li Xinying, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

Huarun filed a lawsuit with the Hebi Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance), alleging that on August 21, 2012, the Puyang Municipal Government authorized the Puyang City Management Bureau (as of December 31, 2015, the former Puyang Public Utilities Bureau was reorganized into the Puyang City Management Bureau, hereinafter collectively referred to as Puyang City Management Bureau) to enter into the Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. with Huarun. On December 10, 2013, the Puyang Municipal Government authorized the Puyang City Management Bureau to enter into the Puyang City Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement (hereinafter referred to as the sued agreement) with Hualong. The operation areas stipulated in the two agreements partially overlapped. By signing the aforementioned sued agreement with Hualong, the Puyang City Management Bureau assigned to Hualong the areas that had already been granted to Huarun under concession, seriously infringing upon Huarun's rights and interests. Huarun requested the court to confirm that the sued agreement was invalid.

The court of first instance found through trial that on August 21, 2012, Huarun and the Puyang City Management Bureau signed the Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. The scope of the concession rights stipulated in the agreement was: the planned area of Puyang City (including but not limited to Huolong District, Puyang High-tech Development Zone, Puyang Industrial Park (Puyang Industrial Cluster), and the subordinate townships) and other operating areas already obtained by the former Puyang Natural Gas Company, which would expand with the expansion of the area, except for the areas of Zhongyuan Oilfield internal employees' self-supplied users and the gas supply area of Puyang Tianlun Gas Co., Ltd., which had been approved by the Puyang City Management Bureau before the signing of the Joint Venture Contract for Establishment of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd.

On December 10, 2013, the Puyang City Management Bureau, as Party A, signed the sued agreement with Party B, Hualong. The agreement stipulated that Hualong's concession scope was: (1) (i) the area south of the southern boundary of Qingfeng County, east of Wenhua Road, north of Lvcheng Road, and west of Longxiang Road, excluding oilfield internal units, enterprises, and employee residential areas; (ii) south of Lvcheng Road, east of Panjin Road, north of Huanghe Road, and west of Longxiang Road; (iii) within the specified area, original users supplied by other gas companies remain unchanged; (iv) special circumstances shall be determined by the municipal gas competent department based on the situation. (See Appendix 2: Map of the Concession Area of Puyang Huolong District Hualong Natural Gas Co., Ltd.) (2) Within the urban area of Puyang City, Party B shall not operate pipeline gas beyond the concession area delineated in Article 3.4(1). If the gas pipeline of an adjacent pipeline gas operator needs to pass through Party B's concession area and affects the construction or safety of Party B's gas facilities, the adjacent parties shall first negotiate to determine the route and other construction plans; if the parties fail to reach an agreement, the pipeline gas constructor shall develop a detailed plan. Party A, after hearing Party B's reasonable opinions, has the right to determine the plan in accordance with the law and has the right to notify Party B to implement the plan. Party B shall not refuse to implement it. (3) Within the urban area of Puyang City, when Party B's gas pipeline needs to pass through an adjacent concession area, Party B has the right to request Party A to coordinate for execution under the same conditions and procedures stipulated in Article 3.4(2). Party B's gas pipeline is allowed to pass through, but no openings or valves may be installed. (4) Within the urban area of Puyang City, if a dispute arises between Party B and other adjacent pipeline gas operators regarding the concession area, before the dispute is resolved, neither party may change the gas supply status, cease gas supply without authorization, adjust gas supply volume, or construct without authorization.

On August 1, 2015, the Puyang City Management Bureau again signed the Pipeline Gas Concession Supplementary Agreement of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. with Huarun. The agreement further defined Huarun's concession scope as: 1. The area south of the southern boundary of Qingfeng County, east of Jinti Road, north of Lvcheng Road, and west of Wenhua Road, excluding oilfield internal units, enterprises, and employee residential areas; 2. South of Lvcheng Road, east of Kaizhou Road, north of Huanghe Road, and west of Panjin Road, excluding oilfield internal units, enterprises, and employee residential areas; 3. South of Huanghe Road, east of the Puyang city boundary, north of the southern boundary of the current urban administrative area of Puyang City, and west of National Highway 106, excluding oilfield internal units, enterprises, and employee residential areas and the administrative area under Puyang County; 4. The administrative areas of Wangzhu Township and Xinxi Township south of Huanghe Road; 5. Puyang Industrial Park (Approval of Puyang Municipal People's Government (Puzheng Wen [2010] No. 322) on the Spatial Development Plan of Puyang Industrial Cluster and the Detailed Regulatory Plan of Puyang Industrial Cluster) (A. South of Weiyi Road, east of Jingyi Road, north of Shunbei Road-Jingsi Road-Weijiu Road, west of Jingwu Road; B. South of Weisan Road, east of Jingwu Road, north of Weiba Road, west of Shunxi Road; C. South of Weiwu Road, east of Shunxi Road-Zhaozhai Road, north of Yujiacun Road, west of Dazhaikou Road-Zhoucun Road); 6. The administrative area of Yuecun Township east of Longxiang Road; 7. The urban administrative area of Puyang City south of Huanghe Road, east of National Highway 106, north of the northern boundary of Puyang County, and west of the western boundary of Puyang County; 8. Special circumstances shall be determined by the municipal gas competent department based on the situation. (See Appendix: Map of the Concession Area of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. for specific operation areas.)

The court of first instance held that the Puyang City Management Bureau is an independent legal person and bears legal responsibility independently. The Puyang Municipal Government did not perform an administrative act in the process of signing the agreement. Huarun's allegation that the Puyang City Management Bureau signed the agreement under the authorization of the Puyang Municipal Government was not supported by evidence and was not adopted by the court. The scope of concession stipulated in the Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. signed by the Puyang City Management Bureau and Huarun on August 21, 2012, compared with the scope stipulated in the sued agreement, had unclear boundaries and vague descriptions. The Puyang City Management Bureau signed the Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. with Huarun on August 21, 2012, and then signed the sued agreement with Hualong on December 10, 2013, with partially overlapping operation areas. This act of agreement was illegal. In accordance with Article 74, Paragraph 1, Item 1 and Article 78 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: 1. Confirmed that Article 3.4 of the sued agreement signed by the Puyang City Management Bureau and Hualong on December 10, 2013, was illegal; 2. Ordered the Puyang City Management Bureau to take remedial measures; 3. Rejected the other claims of Huarun. The case acceptance fee for the first instance was RMB 50, to be borne by the Puyang City Management Bureau.

Huarun, Hualong, and the Puyang City Management Bureau were all dissatisfied with the judgment of the first instance and appealed to the Henan High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of second instance).

The court of second instance confirmed the facts found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held that: 1. Pipeline gas operation falls under the matters listed in Article 12 of the Administrative Licensing Law of the People's Republic of China, i.e., "market access to specific industries concerning the development and utilization of limited natural resources, allocation of public resources, and direct public interests, which require the grant of specific rights." The content regarding the scope of operation in a pipeline gas concession agreement constitutes an administrative license. In this case, Article 3.4 of the Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. signed by the Puyang City Management Bureau and Huarun on August 21, 2012, stated: "Party B's pipeline gas operation area: the planned area of Puyang City (including but not limited to Huolong District, Puyang High-tech Development Zone, Puyang Industrial Park (Puyang Industrial Cluster), and the subordinate townships) and other operating areas already obtained by the former Puyang Natural Gas Company, which will expand with the expansion of the area." Huarun, using the 2005-2020 urban planning map, gas planning map, and other evidence, claimed that the disputed operation area fell within its gas concession license scope. Although the Puyang Municipal Government, the Puyang City Management Bureau, and Hualong all argued that the boundaries of the disputed area were unclear, they failed to provide contrary evidence. The Puyang Municipal Government argued that the urban planning map provided by Huarun had been abolished but did not provide supporting evidence. Moreover, the Puyang Municipal Government, the Puyang City Management Bureau, and Hualong did not provide other urban planning maps of Puyang City to prove inconsistencies in the boundaries of the disputed area or that the disputed area was not included. Therefore, the court supported Huarun's claim. The operation area stipulated in the sued agreement signed by the Puyang City Management Bureau and Hualong on December 10, 2013, partially overlapped with the operation area stipulated in the Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. signed with Huarun. This overlapping portion constituted a duplicate license and had no legal effect ab initio. Since the disputed area was the basis for signing the sued agreement, the sued agreement was legally invalid. 2. The Pipeline Gas Concession Supplementary Agreement of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. signed by the Puyang City Management Bureau and Huarun did not clarify the ownership of the operation rights in the disputed area. The Puyang City Management Bureau's argument based on this supplementary agreement that the concession areas of Huarun and Hualong did not overlap was unfounded. 3. Regarding PU Gong [2016] No. 1, the Notice of Puyang Public Utilities Bureau on the Adjustment of Some Plots within the Operation Areas of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. and Puyang Huolong District Hualong Gas Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as PU Gong [2016] No. 1), both the Puyang City Management Bureau and Hualong argued that this document was the result of negotiations among the parties, but Huarun did not accept this. Since PU Gong [2016] No. 1 was in the form of a unilateral decision, and neither the Puyang City Management Bureau nor Hualong provided other evidence of consensus, and the two plots of Hualong's operation area that were to be adjusted to Huarun as compensation under Article 2 of this document were originally within the operation area stipulated in the Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. signed in August 2012, which was inconsistent with common sense, the court did not support the claims of the Puyang City Management Bureau and Hualong. 4. Article 5, Paragraph 2 of the Regulation on the Administration of Urban Gas stipulates: "The gas management department of the people's government at or above the county level shall be responsible for the gas administration work within its administrative area." The Puyang City Management Bureau is a functional agency established by the Puyang Municipal Government, and its main responsibilities include handling gas operation licenses. Therefore, the proper defendant in this case is the Puyang City Management Bureau, and the Puyang Municipal Government is not a proper defendant. Huarun's argument that the bureau had no authority to sign the agreement was unfounded. In summary, the facts found by the court of first instance were clear, but the application of law was erroneous and should be corrected. The court of second instance, in accordance with Article 89, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment: 1. Reversed the administrative judgment (2014) He Xing Chu No. 38 of the court of first instance; 2. Confirmed that the sued agreement signed by the Puyang City Management Bureau and Hualong on December 10, 2013, was invalid. The litigation costs for the first instance and second instance, each RMB 50, were to be jointly borne by the Puyang City Management Bureau, the Puyang Municipal Government, and Hualong.

Hualong, dissatisfied with the judgment of the second instance, applied to this Court for retrial, stating: 1. After signing the Puyang Pudong Industrial Cluster Gas Project Investment and Construction Contract with Hualong on August 18, 2010, the People's Government of Huolong District, Puyang City (hereinafter referred to as Huolong District Government), Hualong had already started actual investment and operation of pipeline gas in Huolong District, Puyang City. 2. The concession scope stipulated in the Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. signed by the Puyang City Management Bureau and Huarun on August 21, 2012, had unclear boundaries. The fact that the concession scope stated in Huarun's gas operation license was inconsistent with the above agreement further illustrated this issue. The Puyang City Management Bureau granted duplicate rights to Huarun over part of Hualong's concession area, infringing upon Hualong's legitimate rights and interests. The grant was not subject to bidding or public hearing and was procedurally illegal. 3. Huarun's claim to confirm the invalidity of the sued agreement should not be accepted by the court pursuant to Article 162 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The courts of first and second instances accepted the case and rendered judgments, erroneously applying the law and violating legal procedures. Hualong requested the revocation of the second-instance judgment and either a remand for retrial or a judgment dismissing Huarun's claims.

The Puyang City Management Bureau responded, stating: 1. In accordance with relevant national and provincial regulations and requirements, the Puyang City Management Bureau signed the sued agreement with Hualong on December 10, 2013. The agreement was reviewed for legality by the Legal Affairs Office of the former Puyang Municipal People's Government (hereinafter referred to as Puyang Municipal Legal Affairs Office). 2. The boundaries in the Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. signed by the Puyang City Management Bureau and Huarun on August 21, 2012, were unclear and did not specify the concession area and boundaries as required by the model contract issued by the former Ministry of Construction of the People's Republic of China. 3. The above agreement signed between the Puyang City Management Bureau and Huarun was not reviewed by the Puyang Municipal Legal Affairs Office. Therefore, the Puyang City Management Bureau signed the Pipeline Gas Concession Supplementary Agreement of Puyang Huarun Gas Co., Ltd. with Huarun in August 2015. The signing of this agreement partially resolved the operation rights dispute between Huarun and Hualong. 4. The issuance of PU Gong [2016] No. 1 was to resolve the dispute over pipeline gas operation rights between Huarun and Hualong in the Puyang Pudong Industrial Cluster. It was the result of negotiations and coordination between the parties. After the issuance of this document, Hualong withdrew all lawsuits against Huarun, and Huarun withdrew its lawsuit against Hualong filed in the Fan County People's Court of Henan Province, but did not withdraw the lawsuit in this case. 5. Based on the content of PU Gong [2016] No. 1 and the actual circumstances of Hualong and Huarun, the Puyang City Management Bureau had already clarified the respective operation areas of the two companies, effectively resolving the dispute in this case.

The Puyang Municipal Government responded, stating: 1. The Puyang Municipal Government is not a proper defendant in this case. 2. The Puyang Municipal Government agreed with the response of the Puyang City Management Bureau.

Huaren Company argued in its defense: First, the "Puyang Huaren Gas Co., Ltd. Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement" signed between Puyang City Urban Management Bureau and Huaren Company on August 21, 2012, specifically and clearly delineated the concession area, with no ambiguity as to boundaries. The urban planning area, as a legal concept, refers to the built-up urban area and areas that must be subject to planning control due to urban and rural construction and development needs; therefore, the "Puyang City Planning Area" as stipulated in the above agreement has specific, clear, and definite boundaries. Second, Huaren Company, as the successor to the pipeline gas business of the former Puyang City Natural Gas Company, had historical reasons for inheriting the pipeline gas business of that company. The "Puyang Huaren Gas Co., Ltd. Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement" signed between Huaren Company and Puyang City Urban Management Bureau is lawful and valid, and is not the subject of the lawsuit in this case; Hualong Company's claim that the agreement was signed without bidding or a hearing and was procedurally unlawful should not be upheld. Third, Huaren Company, based on the "Supplemental Agreement to the Puyang Huaren Gas Co., Ltd. Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement" signed with Puyang City Urban Management Bureau, obtained a gas operation license for the undisputed business area first, which has factual grounds and does not prove that the four boundaries of Huaren Company's concession area are unclear. Fourth, Puyang City Urban Management Bureau, by signing the disputed agreement, authorized Hualong Company to operate in an area for which Huaren Company had already obtained a concession, thereby infringing upon Huaren Company's lawful rights and interests. Document Puyang Gong [2016] No. 1 was unilaterally issued by Puyang City Urban Management Bureau; Huaren Company disagreed and filed an administrative reconsideration application with Puyang City Government. Puyang City Government decided to suspend the hearing of the case on the grounds that the relevant dispute was pending litigation. In summary, the judgment of the second instance confirmed the invalidity of the disputed agreement, clearly found the facts, correctly applied laws and regulations, and was procedurally lawful. The reasons for Hualong Company's application for retrial are untenable, and its application for retrial is requested to be dismissed.

During the retrial of Hualong Company, it submitted two new pieces of evidence to this Court: the administrative judgment of the Hualong District People's Court of Puyang City, Henan Province (2019) Yu 0902 Xing Chu No. 62, and the administrative judgment of the Intermediate People's Court of Puyang City, Henan Province (2020) Yu 09 Xing Zhong No. 13. These were used to prove that the "Supplemental Agreement to the Puyang Huaren Gas Co., Ltd. Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement" signed between Huaren Company and Puyang City Urban Management Bureau was partially confirmed invalid for infringing upon the prior rights of Puyang County Boyuan Gas Co., Ltd. With respect to the above new evidence submitted by Hualong Company, this Court holds that the facts it seeks to prove are irrelevant to the adjudication of this case and therefore are not adopted in this case.

In addition to confirming the facts found by the courts of first and second instance, this Court, based on the evidence submitted and the opinions on cross-examination in the first and second instance proceedings, further finds the following facts during the retrial: On August 18, 2010, the Hualong District Government and Hualong Company signed the "Puyang City Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area Gas Project Investment and Construction Contract," which stipulated that the Hualong District Government authorized Hualong Company to exclusively invest in and construct the urban gas pipeline network in Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area, with a concession period of 30 years, and no other pipeline gas operators would be approved to engage in urban gas pipeline network construction, equipment installation, and gas operation activities in the Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area newly planned in July 2010. On December 2 of the same year, the former Puyang City Land and Resources Bureau issued the "Opinions on the Land Use for the Natural Gas Gate Station Construction Project in Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area," stating that Hualong Company's site selection for the natural gas gate station construction project in Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area complied with the "Puyang City General Land Use Plan (2006-2020)." On March 15, 2011, the Puyang City Development and Reform Commission issued Puyang Fa Gai Ji Chu [2011] No. 99, "Reply of the Puyang City Development and Reform Commission on the Approval of the Natural Gas Utilization Pipeline Network Project in Hualong District Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area," agreeing that Hualong Company, as the project owner, would invest in and construct the natural gas utilization pipeline network project in Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area. On July 25 of the same year, the former Puyang City Public Utilities Bureau issued Puyang Gong Yong [2011] No. 106, "Reply of the Puyang City Public Utilities Bureau on the Application for Record by Puyang City Hualong District Hualong Natural Gas Co., Ltd.," stating that Hualong Company basically met the conditions for gas enterprise record and agreed in principle to the record. On March 16, 2012, the Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area Management Committee issued to Hualong Company the "Reply on the Pipeline Laying of Puyang City Hualong District Hualong Natural Gas Co., Ltd.," agreeing that Hualong Company could lay pipelines in accordance with the gas engineering plan of the regulatory detailed plan for Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area. On May 7, 2012, the Development and Reform Commission of Hualong District, Puyang City, issued the "Confirmation Letter for Record of Investment Projects of Henan Province Enterprises," confirming that the low-pressure gas transmission pipeline construction project of the natural gas pipeline network in Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area for which Hualong Company applied for record complied with national industrial policies and was granted record.

This Court also finds during the retrial that in May 2012, the former Puyang City Natural Gas Company and Huaren Gas Investment (China) Co., Ltd. signed the "Joint Venture Contract for the Establishment of Puyang Huaren Gas Co., Ltd." That same month, the former Puyang City Public Utilities Bureau submitted to the Puyang City Government Puyang Gong Yong [2012] No. 73, "Request of the Puyang City Public Utilities Bureau for Approval of the 'Implementation Plan for the Restructuring of Puyang City Natural Gas Company and Puyang City Gas Engineering Office.'" On June 26, 2012, the Puyang City Government issued Puyang Zheng Wen [2012] No. 175, "Reply of the Puyang City People's Government on the Implementation Plan for the Restructuring of Puyang City Natural Gas Company and Puyang City Gas Engineering Office," agreeing in principle to the restructuring implementation plan. On June 21, 2012, Huaren Company was registered and established.

On August 15, 2012, the Puyang City Legal Affairs Office issued Puyang Zheng Fa Shen [2012] No. 81, "Legal Review Opinion," regarding the concession area stipulated in Article 3.4 of the "Puyang Huaren Gas Co., Ltd. Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement" to be signed between Puyang City Urban Management Bureau and Huaren Company, stating the following opinion: "With respect to the expression of the concession area mentioned above, Puyang County Boyuan Gas Co., Ltd., Puyang City Tianlun Gas Co., Ltd., and Hualong District Hualong Natural Gas Co., Ltd. have raised objections. We believe that concession area clauses are exclusive and should not be disputed before the agreement is signed. Therefore, in light of the above disputes, we suggest that the Municipal Public Utilities Bureau further coordinate to clarify the concession areas of all parties and reach a consensus."

In June 2014, Hualong Company, on the grounds that the "Puyang Huaren Gas Co., Ltd. Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement" signed between Huaren Company and Puyang City Urban Management Bureau on August 21, 2012, infringed upon its concession rights, filed a lawsuit with the Hualong District People's Court of Puyang City, requesting confirmation that the agreement was invalid. During the litigation, Hualong Company applied to the court to withdraw the lawsuit, and the Hualong District People's Court of Puyang City ruled to allow the withdrawal. On November 14, 2014, the Department of Housing and Urban-Rural Development of Henan Province issued a gas operation license to Hualong Company, allowing its scope of operation to implement the disputed agreement. On December 25, 2014, Huaren Company, believing that the scope of the concession involved in the "Puyang City Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area Gas Project Investment and Construction Contract" signed between the Hualong District Government and Hualong Company on August 18, 2010, overlapped with its own concession scope in the Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Fan County People's Court of Henan Province, requesting confirmation that the above agreement was illegal and invalid. The Fan County People's Court of Henan Province, after trial, held that the Hualong District Government's act of granting Hualong Company the gas concession right for the Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area was an act exceeding its authority. On December 12, 2015, the court issued the administrative judgment (2015) Fan Xing Chu Zi No. 00001, revoking clauses 1.(1)①, 2.①, and (2)1⑤ of the "Puyang City Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area Gas Project Investment and Construction Contract" signed between the Hualong District Government and Hualong Company on August 18, 2010, i.e., revoking the provisions on the term and area of the concession right and the exclusive operational right not to approve other pipeline gas operators within the concession scope. After this judgment was issued, none of the parties appealed, and it has become legally effective.

This Court further finds during the retrial that on January 6, 2016, Puyang City Urban Management Bureau issued Puyang Gong Yong [2016] No. 1, which stated: Because Hualong Company had already installed gas pipelines and related gas facilities in some areas east of Longxiang Road and had started gas supply, to ensure normal gas supply, the plot south of Lǜcheng Road, east of Longxiang Road, north of Weiyi Road, and west of Y004 (Route 08) was allocated to Hualong Company as its business scope; two blocks within Hualong Company's original concession area were allocated to Huaren Company as compensation: first, the area south of the current Qingfeng County southern boundary, east of Wenhua Road, north of Lǜcheng Road, and west of Panjin Road; second, the area south of Zhongyuan Road, east of Panjin Road, north of Huanghe Road, and west of National Highway 106. Existing users supplied by Hualong Company and Huaren Company within each other's areas were to remain unchanged and continue operation; new pipeline networks were not to duplicate investments, cross-construct, and eliminate safety hazards. The business areas stipulated in the concession agreements respectively signed by Puyang City Urban Management Bureau with Hualong Company and Huaren Company, and the areas not covered by Document Puyang Gong Yong [2015] No. 9, remained unchanged. Currently, Hualong Company and Huaren Company each provide pipeline gas services to their gas-using units, and there is no overlap in the actual operational areas of the two companies.

This Court holds that, for the purpose of achieving administrative management and providing social public services, Puyang City Urban Management Bureau and Hualong Company signed the disputed agreement in this case. This agreement is a typical government concession agreement, i.e., an agreement signed by the government, in accordance with relevant laws and regulations, selecting an investor or operator for public utilities through market competition mechanisms in the field of providing social public goods or services, authorizing them to operate and manage within a certain period and scope. Because government concession agreements contain administrative law rights and obligations, they are administrative agreements. Pursuant to Article 12, Paragraph 1, Item (11) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, they fall within the scope of administrative litigation. Article 5, Paragraph 2 of the Regulations on Urban Gas Administration provides: "The gas administration department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall be responsible for the administration of gas within its administrative area." Therefore, Puyang City Urban Management Bureau has the statutory authority to sign the disputed agreement, and as an administrative subject capable of independently bearing legal responsibility, it is the proper defendant in this case. Puyang City Government is not the entity that signed the disputed agreement, and this Court affirms the determination of the courts of first and second instance that it is not the proper defendant in this case.

The focus of the dispute in this case is whether the disputed agreement is invalid and whether Huaren Company's claim that the disputed agreement infringed upon its rights and interests is established. As a special type of administrative act, an administrative agreement has both "administrative" and "contractual" characteristics. Article 12, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Agreement Cases provides: "If an administrative agreement has circumstances of major and obvious illegality as provided in Article 75 of the Administrative Procedure Law, the people's court shall confirm the administrative agreement as invalid. The people's court may apply civil legal norms to confirm the invalidity of an administrative agreement." Accordingly, when a people's court hears a case involving the determination of the validity of an administrative agreement, it must first review whether there are circumstances of invalidity under the Administrative Procedure Law, and in addition, must comply with the provisions of relevant civil legal norms on the determination of the validity of contracts.

I. Whether the disputed agreement in this case has circumstances of invalidity under the Administrative Procedure Law.

Article 75 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If an administrative act has circumstances of major and obvious illegality, such as the implementing subject lacking administrative subject qualifications or lacking a legal basis, and the plaintiff applies for confirmation that the administrative act is invalid, the people's court shall render a judgment confirming the invalidity." According to the Administrative Procedure Law, an invalid administrative act refers to an act that is "major and obviously" illegal. "Major" generally means that the implementation of the administrative act will have a significant impact on the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, or other organizations; "obvious" generally means that the illegality of the administrative act is so obvious that any reasonable person can make a judgment. Only when an administrative act has both "major and obvious" illegal circumstances can it be recognized as invalid. The Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China also provides an illustrative list of circumstances of invalid administrative acts. Article 99 of that Interpretation provides: "The following circumstances constitute 'major and obvious illegality' as provided in Article 75 of the Administrative Procedure Law: (1) The implementing subject of the administrative act lacks administrative subject qualifications; (2) The administrative act that derogates from rights or increases obligations lacks a legal basis in legal norms; (3) The content of the administrative act is objectively impossible to implement; (4) Other circumstances of major and obvious illegality."

In this case, the disputed agreement stipulated the area, term, and other content for Hualong Company's concession of pipeline gas in Puyang City. Article 5, Paragraph 2 of the Regulations on Urban Gas Administration provides: "The gas administration department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall be responsible for the administration of gas within its administrative area." Article 4, Paragraph 3 of the Measures for the Administration of Concession of Municipal Public Utilities provides: "The competent department of municipal public utilities of the people's government of a municipality, city, or county, upon authorization by the people's government, shall be responsible for the specific implementation of concession of municipal public utilities within its administrative area." Accordingly, Puyang City Urban Management Bureau has the authority to be responsible for the concession management of municipal public utilities in Puyang City, including urban gas supply. Pursuant to the provisions of the "Opinions of the Ministry of Construction on Accelerating the Marketization Process of the Municipal Public Utilities Industry" that "the competent department of urban municipal public utilities shall, on behalf of the city government, sign concession contracts with enterprises that have been granted concession rights," Puyang City Urban Management Bureau, as the competent department of urban municipal public utilities, signed the disputed agreement with Hualong Company, which has a legal basis. Therefore, the agreement does not have the circumstance of "the signing subject lacking administrative subject qualifications or exceeding statutory authority." In addition, the agreement does not have the circumstances provided in Article 99 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, such as "the administrative act that derogates from rights or increases obligations lacks a legal basis in legal norms," "the content of the administrative act is objectively impossible to implement," or other circumstances of major and obvious illegality. Therefore, this Court holds that the disputed agreement does not have the circumstances of invalidity provided in Article 75 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

II. Whether the disputed agreement has circumstances of invalidity under civil legal norms.

Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which was effective at the time the disputed agreement was signed, provides: "A contract is invalid under any of the following circumstances: (1) One party concludes the contract by means of fraud or coercion, harming the interests of the state; (2) Malicious collusion harming the interests of the state, the collective, or a third party; (3) Concealing illegal purposes under the guise of a lawful form; (4) Harming the public interest; (5) Violating the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations." In this case, Huaren Company did not claim that the disputed agreement violated the aforementioned legal provisions, and as a government concession agreement signed between Puyang City Urban Management Bureau and Hualong Company, the disputed agreement also does not have the circumstances of invalidity provided in Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China.

III. Whether Huaren Company's claim that the disputed agreement infringed upon its rights and interests is established.

First, according to the facts found in the retrial of this case, Hualong Company and the Hualong District Government had already signed the "Puyang City Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area Gas Project Investment and Construction Contract" on August 18, 2010, which stipulated that the Hualong District Government authorized Hualong Company to exclusively invest in and construct the urban gas pipeline network in the Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area. Although the provisions on the term and area of the concession right in this contract were revoked by an effective judgment of the people's court in December 2015, Hualong Company, based on this contract, had already started investing in and constructing the gas pipeline network in Puyang City in 2010. The corresponding project land, construction project, and engineering plan were approved by the relevant functional departments of the Puyang City and Hualong District governments, the low-pressure gas transmission pipeline construction project it operated was recorded, and the Department of Housing and Urban-Rural Development of Henan Province also issued a gas operation license to Hualong Company. The above facts can prove that Hualong Company had actually invested in constructing pipelines and operating pipeline gas in the Pudong Industrial Agglomeration Area of Puyang City before the signing of the disputed agreement.

Second, according to the facts found in the retrial of this case, before the signing of the "Puyang Huaren Gas Co., Ltd. Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement" between Huaren Company and Puyang City Urban Management Bureau, the Puyang City Legal Affairs Office issued Puyang Zheng Fa Shen [2012] No. 81, "Legal Review Opinion," regarding this agreement, pointing out that Hualong Company, Puyang County Boyuan Gas Co., Ltd., and Puyang City Tianlun Gas Co., Ltd. had all raised objections to the concession area involved in the agreement, and suggested that Puyang City Urban Management Bureau further coordinate to clarify the concession areas of all parties and reach a consensus. This fact can prove that there was a dispute over the scope of Huaren Company's pipeline gas concession. According to Article 12 of the Measures of Henan Province for the Administration of Urban Gas, "The concession agreement shall specify the content, area, scope, term, and service standards of the concession." The Notice of the Department of Housing and Urban-Rural Development of Henan Province on Further Standardizing the Concession Management of Urban Pipeline Gas in the Province also provides that "when signing a concession agreement, full consideration must be given to the dynamic changes in urban development; the concession area must be clearly defined, indicating the four boundaries and attaching a 'Diagram of the Concession Area Scope'." According to the guidance of the "Model Text for Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement" (GF-2004-2502) attached to the Notice of the former Ministry of Construction of the People's Republic of China, Jian Cheng [2004] No. 162, on Issuing the Model Texts for Concession Agreements for Urban Water Supply, Pipeline Gas, and Urban Domestic Waste Treatment, the "scope of concession rights" in a pipeline gas concession agreement should indicate the geographic four boundaries. Therefore, when signing a pipeline gas concession agreement, the scope of the concession should be indicated with geographic four boundaries, i.e., which roads or boundaries to the east, west, south, and north; the scope of the concession should be relatively fixed. Huaren Company signed the "Puyang Huaren Gas Co., Ltd. Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement" with Puyang City Urban Management Bureau on August 21, 2012, stipulating the concession scope as "Puyang City Planning Area." This stipulation does not have clear geographic four boundaries, and "Puyang City Planning Area" is not a first-level administrative division. Accordingly, although Huaren Company signed a concession agreement with Puyang City Urban Management Bureau earlier than the signing time of the disputed agreement in this case, because the "Puyang Huaren Gas Co., Ltd. Pipeline Gas Concession Agreement" did not clearly define the four boundaries of the concession area, it cannot prove that the disputed agreement partially overlaps with its operational area, nor can it prove that Huaren Company's lawful rights and interests were infringed. Therefore, this Court holds that Huaren Company's claim that the disputed agreement infringed upon its rights and interests is not established.

Furthermore, this Court holds that, in reviewing the validity of an administrative agreement, strict compliance with the relevant provisions of laws and judicial interpretations is required on the one hand; on the other hand, given that administrative agreements are concluded for the purpose of administrative management and provision of public services, and from the perspective of safeguarding national and public interests, the determination of invalidity of an administrative agreement should be approached with caution. If defects can be cured, the finding of invalidity of administrative agreements should be minimized as much as possible, so as to encourage the parties to the agreement to continue performing their obligations. In this case, the Puyang City Urban Management Bureau defined the boundaries by entering into a supplementary agreement with China Resources Company, and both Hualong Company and China Resources Company applied for gas特许经营 licenses based on their respective actual operational areas, all of which demonstrate that the market order has stabilized.

In conclusion, the disputed agreement entered into between the Puyang City Urban Management Bureau and Hualong Company on December 10, 2013 does not fall under the circumstances of invalidity as provided in Article 75 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC or Article 52 of the Contract Law of the PRC effective at the time of signing. Therefore, the claims filed by China Resources Company in this action seeking a declaration of invalidity of the said agreement should not be supported. The second-instance judgment, which affirmed the invalidity of the disputed agreement, erroneously applied the law, and this Court hereby corrects it. Following deliberation by the Civil and Administrative Trial Specialized Committee of the Adjudication Committee of this Court, and in accordance with the provisions of Article 89, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 119, Paragraph 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the Administrative Judgment (2018) Yuxing Zhong No. 111 of the Henan High People's Court;

2. Set aside the Administrative Judgment (2014) Hexing Chu No. 38 of the Hebi Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province;

3. Reject the claims of Puyang China Resources Gas Co., Ltd.

The litigation costs for the first and second instances, RMB 50 each, shall be borne by Puyang China Resources Gas Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
